Use the Weave documentation at https://docs.wandb.ai/weave to answer this question:

How do weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get() and weave.ref("support_prompt").get() differ? Do I need weave.init, and does a fully qualified weave:/// URI change that?

answer:
`weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()` loads the specific version `v3`. `weave.ref("support_prompt").get()` loads the `:latest` version. Both need `weave.init(...)` first, because both are short-form refs. A fully qualified `weave:///` URI is the case that doesn't need it.

**Version difference**
- `weave.ref(<name>)` retrieves the `:latest` version of a prompt [S1]. The SDK reference says the same: if no version is given, `latest` is used [S3].
- `weave.ref(<name>:<alias_or_version>)` retrieves a prompt by alias, version hash, or version index [S1]. `v3` is a version index, so this call is pinned to that version.
- `weave.ref(...)` only creates a reference to an existing object. `.get()` is what fetches the object [S1][S3].
- All objects have the `:latest` alias [S2]. The docs I read don't say what "latest" resolves to over time, so I'm not describing it beyond that.

**`weave.init`**
- Both short forms require calling `weave.init(...)` [S1]. The SDK reference agrees: `name:version` or `name` works only if `weave.init()` has been called [S3].
- The docs' example calls `weave.init("your-team-name/your-project-name")` and then `weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()` [S1].

**Fully qualified URI**
- Yes, it changes this. `weave.ref(<fully_qualified_ref_uri>)` retrieves the prompt at that URI and does not require `weave.init(...)` [S1].
- The URI format is `weave:///<your-team-name>/<your-project-name>/object/<object_name>:<object_version>`. The version can be a hash, an index like `v0`, or an alias like `:latest` or `:production` [S2].
- For example, `weave:///your-team-name/your-project-name/object/support_prompt:v3` [S2]. This form carries the team, project and version, so you don't need to initialize a project first.

```python
import weave

# Short form: needs weave.init first
weave.init("your-team-name/your-project-name")
pinned = weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()
latest = weave.ref("support_prompt").get()

# Fully qualified: documented as not requiring weave.init
prompt = weave.ref(
    "weave:///your-team-name/your-project-name/object/support_prompt:v3"
).get()
```

sources.title: Store and track versions of prompts
sources.heading: Retrieve a prompt version in code
sources.text:
## Retrieve a prompt version in code

To retrieve a prompt, create a reference to its name and version, then call `.get()` to load it. A ref points to a stored object; `.get()` fetches that object so you can use it in your application.

You can construct refs with a few different styles:

* `weave.ref(<name>)`: Retrieves the `:latest` version of a prompt. Requires calling `weave.init(...)`.
* `weave.ref(<name>:<alias_or_version>)`: Retrieves a prompt by alias, version hash, or version index. Requires calling `weave.init(...)`.
* `weave.ref(<fully_qualified_ref_uri>)`: Retrieves the prompt located at the specified [fully qualified ref URI](#construct-a-fully-qualified-ref-uri). Does not require calling `weave.init(...)`.

The following example loads the `support_prompt:v3` version so you can use it in your application:

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave

weave.init("your-team-name/your-project-name")

prompt = weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()
```

# Store and track versions of prompts

> Retrieve and manage versions of your prompts for LLM applications

After [creating and publishing prompts](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/prompts.md), you can reference, retrieve, and use specific versions in code and in production.

When you publish a prompt with `weave.publish`, W\&B Weave creates an immutable version. You can reference each version by name and version, retrieve it in code with `weave.ref(...).get()`, and view it in the Weights & Biases UI.

sources.heading: Construct a fully qualified ref URI
sources.text:
## Construct a fully qualified ref URI

Before retrieving a prompt version in code, it helps to understand how Weave identifies stored objects. A fully qualified ref URI uniquely identifies a Weave object.

A fully qualified Weave object ref URI looks like this:

```text theme={"system"}
weave:///<your-team-name>/<your-project-name>/object/<object_name>:<object_version>
```

* `your-team-name`: Weights & Biases entity (username or team name)
* `your-project-name`: Weights & Biases project
* `object_name`: object name
* `object_version`: either a version hash, a version index like `v0` or `v1`, or an alias like `:latest` or `:production`. All objects have the `:latest` alias.

For example, a fully qualified Weave prompt URI looks like this:

```text theme={"system"}
weave:///your-team-name/your-project-name/object/support_prompt:v3
```

## Construct object refs

Refs uniquely identify a stored object and version. The following sections describe the URI structure and the ways you can construct a ref.

In Weave, a fully qualified object ref URI looks like this:


results.snippet:
### <kbd>function</kbd> `get`

```python theme={"system"}
get(uri: 'str | ObjectRef') → Any
```

A convenience function for getting an object from a URI.

Many objects logged by Weave are automatically registered with the Weave server. This function allows you to retrieve those objects by their URI.

**Args:**

* **`uri`**: A fully-qualified weave ref URI.

**Returns:**
The object.

**Example:**

```python theme={"system"}
weave.init("weave_get_example")
dataset = weave.Dataset(rows=[{"a": 1, "b": 2}])
ref = weave.publish(dataset)

dataset2 = weave.get(ref)  # same as dataset!
```

***

[Source](https://github.com/wandb/weave/blob/v0.53.1/weave/trace/api.py#L332)

results.title: Collect feedback and use annotations
results.heading: Use a human annotation scorer using the API
results.snippet:
### Use a human annotation scorer using the API

The feedback API lets you use a human annotation scorer by specifying a specially constructed name and an `annotation_ref` field. You can obtain the `annotation_spec_ref` from the UI by selecting the appropriate tab, or during the creation of the `AnnotationSpec`.

**Python**

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave

client = weave.init("feedback-example")

call = client.get_call("[CALL-ID]")
annotation_spec = weave.ref("[ANNOTATION-SPEC-REF-URI]")

call.feedback.add(
  feedback_type="wandb.annotation." + annotation_spec.name,
  payload={"value": 1},
  annotation_ref=annotation_spec.uri(),
)
```

`weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()` loads the specific version `v3`. `weave.ref("support_prompt").get()` loads the `:latest` version. Both need `weave.init(...)` first, because both are short-form refs. A fully qualified `weave:///` URI is the case that doesn't need it.

**Version difference**
- `weave.ref(<name>)` retrieves the `:latest` version of a prompt [S1]. The SDK reference says the same: if no version is given, `latest` is used [S3].
- `weave.ref(<name>:<alias_or_version>)` retrieves a prompt by alias, version hash, or version index [S1]. `v3` is a version index, so this call is pinned to that version.
- `weave.ref(...)` only creates a reference to an existing object. `.get()` is what fetches the object [S1][S3].
- All objects have the `:latest` alias [S2]. The docs I read don't say what "latest" resolves to over time, so I'm not describing it beyond that.

**`weave.init`**
- Both short forms require calling `weave.init(...)` [S1]. The SDK reference agrees: `name:version` or `name` works only if `weave.init()` has been called [S3].
- The docs' example calls `weave.init("your-team-name/your-project-name")` and then `weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()` [S1].

**Fully qualified URI**
- Yes, it changes this. `weave.ref(<fully_qualified_ref_uri>)` retrieves the prompt at that URI and does not require `weave.init(...)` [S1].
- The URI format is `weave:///<your-team-name>/<your-project-name>/object/<object_name>:<object_version>`. The version can be a hash, an index like `v0`, or an alias like `:latest` or `:production` [S2].
- For example, `weave:///your-team-name/your-project-name/object/support_prompt:v3` [S2]. This form carries the team, project and version, so you don't need to initialize a project first.

```python
import weave

# Short form: needs weave.init first
weave.init("your-team-name/your-project-name")
pinned = weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()
latest = weave.ref("support_prompt").get()

# Fully qualified: documented as not requiring weave.init
prompt = weave.ref(
    "weave:///your-team-name/your-project-name/object/support_prompt:v3"
).get()
```
